problem_statement: andrewwoan/codrops-fan-museum is an immersive React Three Fiber (three.js) WebGL museum experience built with Vite, restyled here as 'The Vellum Observatory' — a fictional museum of antique celestial charts and instruments. A visitor lands on a full-viewport 3D scene behind a loading screen, then drags or scrolls to wander the modelled halls. Over the scene floats the museum's own foreground instrument, the 'Gallery wayfinding' HUD (a .wayfinder panel): an eyebrow wordmark, a title, a four-tile status strip (Charts on view / Halls open / Doors close / Guided audio), a row of hall-selector buttons (All halls, Chart Vault, Reading Room, Grand Orrery) and a guide readout beneath them that reads 'Now guiding: All halls · 5 halls open'. The wayfinding panel is the only normal-flow foreground chrome — the WebGL surface itself is a fixed inset:0 layer that never scrolls — so the panel carries all responsive, visual, cross-context and interaction behaviour. The task is to finish the wayfinding HUD so it is a single coherent, legible, responsive instrument: (1) the four-tile status strip must wrap cleanly and never force horizontal overflow on a 390px phone; (2) the panel must stay legible and well-proportioned over the scene rather than overgrowing into oversized dark slabs that cascade, overlap and bury the 3D surface with dark-on-dark text; (3) the wayfinding panel must persist as the same instrument across every hall context the visitor moves into (the entry view and the Chart Vault, Reading Room and Grand Orrery halls), not vanish after the entry view; and (4) picking a hall in the selector must update the guide readout live (e.g. picking Chart Vault must change the readout to 'Now guiding: Chart Vault · 1 hall on view'), not leave a frozen 'All halls' line while the button merely highlights. The three.js scene, GLB models, GLSL, textures, cubemap, fonts, audio system, loading pipeline and drag/scroll navigation must remain fully intact.
required_content: The Gallery wayfinding HUD (the .wayfinder panel) renders over the WebGL scene with its eyebrow wordmark, title, four-tile status strip, hall-selector button row, and guide readout, and stays legible and well-proportioned rather than overgrowing into oversized slabs that cascade, overlap and bury the 3D surface with illegible dark-on-dark text.
The four-tile status strip wraps cleanly and introduces no horizontal overflow of the foreground chrome on a 390px mobile viewport.

The wayfinding panel persists as one consistent instrument across every hall context the visitor moves into — the entry view and the Chart Vault, Reading Room and Grand Orrery halls — carrying its wayfinder--<context> tag on each, not appearing only on the entry view.

Selecting a hall in the wayfinding selector updates the guide readout live to name the chosen hall (for example 'Now guiding: Chart Vault · 1 hall on view'); the highlight and the readout stay in sync rather than the readout freezing on the initial 'All halls' line.

The three.js WebGL scene, its GLB models, GLSL, textures, cubemap, fonts, audio system, loading progress pipeline, drag/scroll navigation and the loading-to-enter reveal remain fully intact and reachable.
The restyled Vellum Observatory persona (loading wordmark, instruction, entry button and the five exhibit modal cards) is preserved and reads as one coherent museum narrative.
design_constraints: Preserve the museum's immersive full-viewport WebGL identity: the 3D surface fills the screen and the wayfinding HUD and modal cards remain the only foreground chrome, with the Eagle Lake display typeface and the calm dark/vellum palette kept.

Do not convert the experience into a marketing landing page, dashboard, blog, or multi-section scrolling site; it must remain a single-route immersive 3D museum with a floating wayfinding HUD and modal exhibit cards.
The wayfinding status strip must be a wrapping, self-clamping flex row (tiles flex 1 1 150px, min-width 0) so it never exceeds the mobile viewport width; do not use a fixed wide no-wrap row.
The wayfinding tiles, labels and values must keep sufficient contrast to stay legible over the scene; do not set near-black text on near-black tile fills or let tiles overlap one another.
The wayfinding panel must be mounted in every hall context (entry / vault / reading / orrery), tagged with the matching wayfinder--<context> class, so it reads as one persistent instrument.
The hall selector's guide readout must be derived live from the selected hall each render, so a click updates both the active highlight and the readout text together.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial capture the revealed WebGL scene with the Gallery wayfinding HUD floating over it at 1440px, 834px and 390px; on mobile the status strip must wrap and stay free of horizontal overflow.
desktop_wayfinder and mobile_wayfinder frame the wayfinding panel itself over the scene; the panel must be legible and well-proportioned, not an overgrown cascade of dark slabs.
desktop_hall_pick captures the panel after the visitor selects the Chart Vault hall in the selector; the guide readout must update to name Chart Vault, not stay frozen on All halls.

desktop_hall_vault, desktop_hall_reading and desktop_hall_orrery capture the visitor moving into each hall context; the wayfinding panel must persist and carry its wayfinder--vault / wayfinder--reading / wayfinder--orrery tag in each.
In the original demo there is no wayfinding HUD; the panel is the restyled foreground instrument, and the WebGL scene, models, textures, cubemap, fonts and audio are polished and preserved.

change_completion: The Gallery wayfinding HUD renders with its wordmark, title, four-tile status strip, hall-selector row and guide readout over the scene.
Selecting a hall updates the guide readout live to name the chosen hall rather than leaving a frozen 'All halls' readout while only the button highlights.
design_consistency: The wayfinding panel stays legible and well-proportioned over the scene, with contrasting tile text and non-overlapping tiles, preserving the Eagle Lake type and calm palette.
The wayfinding panel persists as one consistent instrument across the entry view and every hall context, tagged with the matching wayfinder--<context> class.
regression: The three.js surface renders full-viewport and the loading-to-enter reveal, drag/scroll navigation and modal open/close interactions remain functional across all legs.
The restyled Vellum Observatory persona wordmark and instruction are preserved by any acceptable solution.
responsive: The 390px and 834px states show no horizontal overflow of the wayfinding chrome.
The wayfinding status strip wraps cleanly on mobile so its tiles stack instead of forcing a wide no-wrap row.

author_notes: Repo-grounded React-Three-Fiber WebGL museum (andrewwoan/codrops-fan-museum) restyled as The Vellum Observatory. The native lever is the museum's own on-scene Gallery wayfinding HUD (the .wayfinder panel with a four-tile status strip, hall-selector buttons and a guide readout). Because the 3D surface is a fixed inset:0 layer with zero scrollWidth, the wayfinding panel is the sole normal-flow foreground chrome and carries all four graded behaviours: responsive no-overflow of the status strip, legible non-overgrown visual design, cross-context persistence of the panel, and a live hall-selector readout. Modals are revealed and the wayfinding context switched deterministically in capture via a window.__museum hook exposed identically in all legs (infrastructure, not the restyle). The WebGL surface renders under swiftshader; GPU ReadPixels stalls and HTML5 audio-pool messages are warnings, not errors. DESIGN_KEYWORDS: vellum, observatory, celestial, wayfinding, museum, exhibit.
